<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

On ROCm, the `deepseek_v32` path (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.x) now skips the sparse indexer's Q projection and scoring for pure short prefills that run on dense MHA. CUDA already skips the scoring (#48407, #51298), and both now use the same check. Builds on the ROCm dense-MHA prefill from #49263.

## Claims

- GLM-5.1-FP8, MI355X, TP4: 1K-token prefill median TTFT -10.7% at c1, -5.0% at c32. On every call it changes, the attention output and KV caches are bit-identical to main. gsm8k unchanged; GPQA-Diamond 0.691 on both main and this PR (8 runs each).
- GLM-5.2-MXFP4 (indexer on 21 of 78 layers): no significant change (measured on the first revision).
- Mixed batches, prefills longer than `index_topk`, MTP layers, FULL cudagraph and capture still score. Other platforms are unchanged.

## Validation

- `test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py`: 36 passed, 8 skipped (7 need SM100, 1 needs the DeepSelect extension) on MI355X. `test_rocm_short_prefill_skips_indexer_q_and_scoring` drives `_fused_attention`: a short dense-MHA prefill runs neither `wq_b` nor the indexer, and `fused_norm_rope` still gets the indexer K cache. pre-commit clean.
- `test_rocm_fused_v32_dense_prefill_matches_mqa` (existing, AMD V1 Attention CI): passed, auto and fp8 KV. Its dense run skips one step whose keys a later 2049+-token decode scores.
- Serving, GLM-5.1-FP8, TP4, output 1 token, 2 runs per arm in order main, v1, PR, PR, v1, main (v1 = first revision, scoring skip only), no failed requests:

| workload | median TTFT (ms), main → v1 → PR | PR vs main |
|---|---|---|
| 1K in, c1 | 165.8 → 150.5 → 148.0 | -10.7% |
| 1K in, c32 | 1949.7 → 1919.0 → 1851.9 | -5.0% |

- gsm8k 5-shot strict / flexible, GLM-5.1-FP8: main 0.9462 / 0.9439, PR 0.9454 / 0.9439 (stderr 0.006).
- GPQA-Diamond (CoT zero-shot, chat template, temperature 0, 12288-token cap), GLM-5.1-FP8, 8 runs per arm, interleaved: main mean 0.691 (0.652-0.737), PR 0.691 (0.646-0.722), stderr 0.033 per run. 59-72 of 198 answers hit the cap in every run. lm_eval sends all 198 questions at once; a step logger showed that only the first prefill step (1-3 prompts) takes the skip, and the other prompts prefill in mixed batches, which run the same code as main. Batching matched across arms: in every logged run, one sparse-MHA prefill step took 60-62 prompts, 57 of them the same in all eight.
- Bitwise check: on every call this PR changes, a probe ran the main path twice and then the PR path on the same inputs, and compared the attention output and both KV caches (MLA and indexer). 13,416 calls on each of the 4 TP ranks (80 greedy requests at c1, the 1K c1 and c32 workloads, and a GPQA burst): all bit-identical, for main vs main and for main vs PR.
- v1 only: 1900 in c1 and 8K in c1 (sparse path) within noise. GLM-5.2-MXFP4, MTP3, 3 runs per arm: TTFT -0.6% to -1.9%, within noise; gsm8k strict 0.9356 → 0.9356, acceptance length 3.31 → 3.31.

<details>
<summary>Per-run numbers, probes, profile and reproduction</summary>

Image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly` (AITER 0.1.25) running main at 7f730b4 and this branch from source, MI355X.

GLM-5.1-FP8 (78 indexer layers, no spec decode), median TTFT in ms:

| run | arm | 1K c1 | 1K c32 | 1K c32 total tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | main | 164.8 | 1949.2 | 16755 |
| E2 | v1 | 152.0 | 1920.0 | 17032 |
| E3 | PR | 148.0 | 1851.2 | 17643 |
| E4 | PR | 148.1 | 1852.6 | 17636 |
| E5 | v1 | 148.9 | 1918.1 | 17037 |
| E6 | main | 166.8 | 1950.3 | 16748 |

GPQA-Diamond runs in order: PR 0.697, main 0.737, main 0.712, PR 0.646, main 0.712, PR 0.687, PR 0.692, main 0.697, then with the step logger main 0.677, PR 0.722, PR 0.692, main 0.682, main 0.652, PR 0.687, PR 0.702, main 0.662. The first eight favor main by 3.4 points and the next eight favor the PR by 3.3. Main is not run-to-run deterministic on this model even at c1: the same 40 greedy requests sent twice to one main server give bit-identical prompt logprobs for 0.3% of values (mean |d| 0.21 nats); main vs PR shows the same 0.21.

A probe on TP rank 0 counted eager indexer-layer calls over the same workloads. On pure dense-MHA prefills, v1 ran `wq_b` and the indexer part of `fused_q` in 7098 of 7098 calls and scored in none; this PR ran none of the three in 7176 calls, and `fused_norm_rope` wrote the indexer K cache in all 7176. Mixed batches (156 calls) and decode (4368) ran all three in both arms.

First revision (v1) against main, earlier sessions:

| run | arm | 1K c1 | 1900 c1 | 1K c32 | 8K c1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | main | 166.5 | 175.8 | 1950.1 | 622.9 |
| F2 | v1 | 149.2 | 174.6 | 1916.9 | 623.1 |
| F3 | v1 | 153.1 | 172.7 | 1919.1 | 623.6 |
| F4 | main | 162.5 | 175.4 | 1947.0 | 617.4 |

v1 gsm8k strict / flexible: main 0.9469 / 0.9462 and 0.9424 / 0.9409, v1 0.9447 / 0.9439 and 0.9462 / 0.9484.

GLM-5.2-MXFP4 (21 indexer layers plus the MTP layer; TTFT runs use MTP3 with synthetic acceptance 3.0), median TTFT in ms, runs in order A B B A A B:

| arm | 1K c1 | 1900 c1 | 1K c32 | 8K c1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 152.4 / 154.3 / 152.8 | 148.9 / 150.3 / 152.2 | 1501.8 / 1503.7 / 1513.2 | 471.6 / 475.7 / 473.0 |
| v1 | 152.0 / 150.6 / 154.1 | 145.7 / 147.4 / 149.5 | 1489.8 / 1492.2 / 1492.2 | 471.8 / 470.5 / 457.9 |

GLM-5.2 gsm8k with real MTP3: strict 0.9356 → 0.9356, flexible 0.9356 → 0.9363, acceptance length 3.310 → 3.311. At concurrency 1 (250 questions, every prefill a pure short prefill): 0.952 → 0.944 (stderr 0.014). A probe on TP rank 0 counted indexer-layer calls on pure dense-MHA prefills: main scored 8382 of 8382, v1 382 of 8404, all on the MTP layer.

Why 1K gains more than 1900 in v1 (GLM-5.1-FP8, TP rank 0). Prefill runs eagerly, and on main the host needs about 148 ms to issue a step at either length. A probe timed the forward without a profiler (median of 20, ms). Host times move by up to 10 ms between sessions with node load; a first main session under heavy load (1K host issue 187 ms) was repeated:

| arm | 1K: host issue / GPU tail after it | 1900: host issue / GPU tail after it |
|---|---|---|
| main | 147.6 / 4.4 | 149.8 / 12.3 |
| v1, run 1 | 131.3 / 6.9 | 131.1 / 27.6 |
| v1, run 2 | 142.0 / 0.4 | 143.4 / 15.3 |

At 1K the GPU finishes within a few ms of the last launch, so the step is host-bound and the indexer's host work shows up in TTFT. At 1900 the GPU runs 12-28 ms past the host; host + tail stays at 159-162 ms in every run, and only the indexer's GPU time is saved. A torch profiler trace per step: v1 removes 312 kernels (4 per layer), 1.43 ms of GPU time at 1K and 2.17 ms at 1900; on main the indexer op costs 190-198 us of host time but 24-34 us of GPU time per call (host time inflated by the profiler).

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MLA=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_RMSNORM=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP8BMM=0 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4BMM=0 \
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8 --tensor-parallel-size 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --max-model-len 16384 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9
# GLM-5.2: amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4, same flags plus
#   --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'

# 1K c1 shown. 1900 c1: --random-input-len 1900 --seed 45.
# 1K c32: --num-prompts 512 --max-concurrency 32 --seed 46.
# 8K c1: --random-input-len 8192 --num-prompts 16 --seed 47.
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8 --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 1 --temperature 0 \
  --num-prompts 40 --max-concurrency 1 --seed 44

lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size 1 \
  --model_args model=zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=64,tokenized_requests=False
lm_eval --model local-chat-completions --tasks gpqa_diamond_cot_zeroshot --apply_chat_template \
  --model_args "model=zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=198,tokenized_requests=False,think_end_token=</think>" \
  --gen_kwargs max_gen_toks=12288

VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 pytest -v tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py \
  "tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py::test_rocm_fused_v32_dense_prefill_matches_mqa"
```

</details>

## Details

- Placement: `DeepseekV32MLAAttention._fused_attention`, which already holds the MLA metadata. CUDA passes the layer name into its op only because the op cannot see that metadata.
- Conditions: `should_skip_indexer_scoring()` in `sparse_attn_indexer.py`, which the CUDA op now also calls, plus the layer taking the dense-MHA branch. The flag in `DeepseekV32Attention` moves from `is_cuda()` to `is_cuda_alike()`.
- K cache: still written by `fused_norm_rope`. The indexer Q projection (`wq_b`), the indexer part of `fused_q` and scoring are dropped.
- The gain at c1 is host time: an eager 1K prefill is host-bound and each indexer call costs about 0.2 ms on the host. Dropping `wq_b` (a 2048 → 32x128 GEMM per layer) also saves GPU time, which shows at c32.
- CI: `vllm/models/deepseek_v32` is added to the source dependencies of the MI300 Model Executor step in `test-amd.yaml`, so that changes there run this test file. `test_areas/model_executor.yaml` has it since #59223.
- Not measured: DeepSeek-V3.2 (same code path), GLM-5.1 with MTP, TP8.

<details>
<summary>Design notes</summary>

- Moving the check into `rocm_aiter_sparse_attn_indexer` would mirror CUDA but add an argument to an op that DeepSeek-V4 shares; the model already has the MLA metadata and the dense-MHA decision.
- The ROCm indexer op is built with `skip_k_cache_insert=True`. `fused_norm_rope` writes the indexer keys and clears the top-k buffer before the decision.
- PCP leaves the flag off, as on CUDA; ROCm sparse MLA rejects DCP. MTP layers keep scoring, as on CUDA.
- This model is not torch.compiled. Prefills run eagerly under the default FULL_DECODE_ONLY; under breakable cudagraphs the eager segment re-evaluates the decision on replay. Profile and dummy runs (no metadata) still call the op, so its workspace is reserved.

</details>

Not a duplicate: no open or closed PR skips indexer scoring on ROCm.

<details>
<summary>Duplicate search</summary>

`gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state all --search` with "short prefill indexer ROCm", "skip indexer ROCm", "indexer scoring ROCm", "dense mha indexer ROCm", "short prefill topk ROCm", "rocm_aiter_sparse_attn_indexer", "dense_mha_metadata_layer_name", "short prefill skip indexer", "GLM ROCm indexer prefill", "ROCm DSv3.2 indexer". Nearest: #56944 and #60601 (shard indexer prefill rows across TP), #61504 (sparse MLA decode indptr), #60294 (aiter `mqa_logits` for indexer prefill); none skips scoring.

</details>

AI assistance (Claude) was used for the implementation, the measurements and this description.

</details>

GLM-5.2 gsm8k with real MTP3: strict 0.9356 → 0.9356, flexible 0.9356 → 0.9363, acceptance length 3.310 → 3.311. At concurrency 1 (250 questions, every prefill a pure short prefill): 0.952 → 0.944 (stderr 0.014). A probe on TP rank 0 counted indexer-layer calls on pure dense-MHA prefills: main scored 8382 of 8382, v1 382 of 8404, all on the MTP layer.

Why 1K gains more than 1900 in v1 (GLM-5.1-FP8, TP rank 0). Prefill runs eagerly, and on main the host needs about 148 ms to issue a step at either length. A probe timed the forward without a profiler (median of 20, ms). Host times move by up to 10 ms between sessions with node load; a first main session under heavy load (1K host issue 187 ms) was repeated:

| arm | 1K: host issue / GPU tail after it | 1900: host issue / GPU tail after it |
|---|---|---|
| main | 147.6 / 4.4 | 149.8 / 12.3 |
| v1, run 1 | 131.3 / 6.9 | 131.1 / 27.6 |
| v1, run 2 | 142.0 / 0.4 | 143.4 / 15.3 |

At 1K the GPU finishes within a few ms of the last launch, so the step is host-bound and the indexer's host work shows up in TTFT. At 1900 the GPU runs 12-28 ms past the host; host + tail stays at 159-162 ms in every run, and only the indexer's GPU time is saved. A torch profiler trace per step: v1 removes 312 kernels (4 per layer), 1.43 ms of GPU time at 1K and 2.17 ms at 1900; on main the indexer op costs 190-198 us of host time but 24-34 us of GPU time per call (host time inflated by the profiler).

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MLA=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_RMSNORM=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP8BMM=0 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4BMM=0 \
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8 --tensor-parallel-size 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --max-model-len 16384 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9
# GLM-5.2: amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4, same flags plus
#   --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'

# 1K c1 shown. 1900 c1: --random-input-len 1900 --seed 45.
# 1K c32: --num-prompts 512 --max-concurrency 32 --seed 46.
# 8K c1: --random-input-len 8192 --num-prompts 16 --seed 47.
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8 --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 1 --temperature 0 \
  --num-prompts 40 --max-concurrency 1 --seed 44

lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size 1 \
  --model_args model=zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=64,tokenized_requests=False
lm_eval --model local-chat-completions --tasks gpqa_diamond_cot_zeroshot --apply_chat_template \
  --model_args "model=zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=198,tokenized_requests=False,think_end_token=</think>" \
  --gen_kwargs max_gen_toks=12288

VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 pytest -v tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py \
  "tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py::test_rocm_fused_v32_dense_prefill_matches_mqa"
```

</details>

## Details

- Placement: `DeepseekV32MLAAttention._fused_attention`, which already holds the MLA metadata. CUDA passes the layer name into its op only because the op cannot see that metadata.
- Conditions: `should_skip_indexer_scoring()` in `sparse_attn_indexer.py`, which the CUDA op now also calls, plus the layer taking the dense-MHA branch. The flag in `DeepseekV32Attention` moves from `is_cuda()` to `is_cuda_alike()`.
- K cache: still written by `fused_norm_rope`. The indexer Q projection (`wq_b`), the indexer part of `fused_q` and scoring are dropped.
- The gain at c1 is host time: an eager 1K prefill is host-bound and each indexer call costs about 0.2 ms on the host. Dropping `wq_b` (a 2048 → 32x128 GEMM per layer) also saves GPU time, which shows at c32.
- CI: `vllm/models/deepseek_v32` is added to the source dependencies of the MI300 Model Executor step in `test-amd.yaml`, so that changes there run this test file. `test_areas/model_executor.yaml` has it since #59223.
- Not measured: DeepSeek-V3.2 (same code path), GLM-5.1 with MTP, TP8.

<details>
<summary>Design notes</summary>

- Moving the check into `rocm_aiter_sparse_attn_indexer` would mirror CUDA but add an argument to an op that DeepSeek-V4 shares; the model already has the MLA metadata and the dense-MHA decision.
- The ROCm indexer op is built with `skip_k_cache_insert=True`. `fused_norm_rope` writes the indexer keys and clears the top-k buffer before the decision.
- PCP leaves the flag off, as on CUDA; ROCm sparse MLA rejects DCP. MTP layers keep scoring, as on CUDA.
- This model is not torch.compiled. Prefills run eagerly under the default FULL_DECODE_ONLY; under breakable cudagraphs the eager segment re-evaluates the decision on replay. Profile and dummy runs (no metadata) still call the op, so its workspace is reserved.

</details>

Not a duplicate: no open or closed PR skips indexer scoring on ROCm.

<details>
<summary>Duplicate search</summary>

`gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state all --search` with "short prefill indexer ROCm", "skip indexer ROCm", "indexer scoring ROCm", "dense mha indexer ROCm", "short prefill topk ROCm", "rocm_aiter_sparse_attn_indexer", "dense_mha_metadata_layer_name", "short prefill skip indexer", "GLM ROCm indexer prefill", "ROCm DSv3.2 indexer". Nearest: #56944 and #60601 (shard indexer prefill rows across TP), #61504 (sparse MLA decode indptr), #60294 (aiter `mqa_logits` for indexer prefill); none skips scoring.

</details>
